title: Annotatio III §.X (3)(b): Instituted praxis — cup as well as bread; Mass/Transsubstantiation snatches the cup from the laity
pass_a_gloss: (b) By Instituted Praxis, insofar as this draws origin immediately from Christ, and by which it binds each Communicant no less to the use of the Cup and wine than of bread — to be snatched meanwhile from all the Laity by the Mass and the rationale of Transsubstantiation. By this pact Transsubstantiation also strikes against the posterior Table of the Divine Law, withdrawing from the Neighbor what Christ by express mandate willed given him through the τὸ: Do this, enjoining on those administering the Sacred Supper that they designate all that He Himself had designated while administering.
pass_b_english: (3)(b) Instituted praxis from Christ binds every communicant to the cup and wine no less than to the bread.
Mass and Transsubstantiation’s rationale snatch that cup from all the laity — so it also hits the second table, withdrawing from the neighbor what Christ ordered by ‘Do this.’
source_text: (b) Praxi Institutæ, quatenus hæc à Christo immediatè originem trahit, quâque non minùs ad Calicis vinique, quam panis usum, singulos Communicantes obstringit, per Missam interim & Transsubstantiationis rationem, Laicis cunctis eripiendum. Hoc pacto Transsubstantiatio etiam in posteriorem Divinæ Legis Tabulam impingit, Proximo id subducens, quod illi tribuendum expresso Christus mandato voluit per τὸ: Hoc facite, S. Coenam administraturis id omne designandum injungens, quod ipse administrans designaverat.
